title: The Phantom of Blackwood Manor
author: AI Weaver
description: In fogbound Blackwood Manor, Lord Reginald Blackwood is found dead in a locked study. Detective Elias Pembroke must untangle a locked-room poison mystery woven through inheritance, debts, and doctored accounts.
intro_narrative: Mist coils around Blackwood Manor as Detective Elias Pembroke arrives to find Lord Reginald Blackwood dead at his desk in a bolted study. The constable whispers of a heart seizure, but the house feels like it is hiding something: a bitter scent in the brandy, grit where it shouldn’t be, and a trail of private meetings that all lead back to money. In a manor full of locked doors and watching portraits, Pembroke must prove there was no phantom—only a patient hand and a common poison.

required_evidence: Mr. Cecil Ashworth’s travel case with a false lining
Torn solicitor’s letter mentioning an audit
Brandy bottle with re-tied twine seal
required_motive: Prevent an impending audit from exposing forged/embezzled estate accounts and personal ruin.

phases.name: Arrival & Crime Scene
phases.objective: Examine the locked study and its immediate surroundings to establish cause of death and the locked-room constraints.

phases.name: Interviews & Motives
phases.objective: Interview the household and guests; identify who had motive, access, and opportunity around the brandy and the study.

phases.name: Hidden Routes & Physical Trail
phases.objective: Follow the gritty mud trail and test house logistics: from yard to passage to library to study; confirm tampering with bottle/seal and records.

phases.name: Confrontation
phases.objective: Assemble evidence, press contradictions, and force a break: connect audit letter + forged ledgers + hidden arsenic to the poisoned brandy.

Blackwood Manor.description: A slate-coloured mass of blackened stone and dripping ivy, its timbers groaning as fog presses close to the high windows. The entire estate feels like a witness that has learned to keep secrets.
clues: Each suspect privately met Lord Blackwood that evening, but only Ashworth had business motive tied directly to the threatened audit.

visual_metadata.setting: Fog, wrought-iron gates, and a long facade of blackened stone. The manor’s sounds—timber groans, chain clicks—create a constant sense of pressure.

The Locked Study.description: Lord Blackwood’s walnut desk and law books surround a slumped body; a low coal fire leaves sour warmth and drifting ash. A shattered decanter glitters on the rug, and the room’s order feels violently interrupted by one careless thumbprint.
clues: The study door was bolted from the inside and the window latched, suggesting the poisoner did not need to escape through either.
A shattered crystal decanter on the rug smelled faintly of bitter almonds, suggesting poison rather than a natural collapse.
A single brandy glass bore a greasy thumb-smudge at the rim inconsistent with Lord Blackwood’s tidy habits.
Mud with fine grit was found on the study hearthstone, unlike the manor’s softer garden soil.

The Corridor Outside the Study.description: A narrow, dark-oak corridor lined with portraits whose varnished eyes trap candlelight. The air is colder toward the east wing, as if the locked door there exhales.
clues: The brandy bottle in the sideboard showed a newly cut twine knot, as though it had been opened and re-tied to look undisturbed.

visual_metadata.setting: Portrait-lined hall with a runner rug; candlelight pools and drafts tug at chains and doors. The study door sits at the end; the east wing barrier feels ominous.

The Drawing Room.description: Velvet curtains shut out the mist; oil lamps cast amber pools across oppressive luxury. A portrait of Lord Blackwood looms over a long sofa like a judge that never adjourns.
clues: Lady Vivienne had argued about inheritance and changed her will, but she had no access to the brandy decanter after dinner.

visual_metadata.setting: Warm but stifling: velvet drapes, oil lamps, and a formal arrangement designed for appearances rather than comfort.

The Library.description: Leather bindings and coal dust create a rich suffocation. A green-shaded lamp lights account books spread like a battlefield where numbers have been wounded and bandaged.
items: Ink blotter and pen from the library writing desk
clues: Mr. Ashworth arrived for “urgent business,” and was seen in the library handling the estate ledgers shortly before dinner.
Forged accounting ledgers in the library showed altered columns and fresh ink matching Ashworth’s blotter and pen-nib wear.

visual_metadata.setting: Dense shelves, a long table with account books, and a writing desk whose blotter bears fresh smears. The room invites quiet tampering.

The Guest Suite.description: A damp, camphor-tinged room where rain taps at the window like restless fingers. Its neatness feels temporary, like a guest trying not to leave a fingerprint on the house.
items: Mr. Cecil Ashworth’s travel case with a false lining
clues: Dr. Hargrove had gambling debts and carried medicines, but his satchel lacked any arsenical preparation and he had treated the household for years without incident.
A vial of arsenic was discovered hidden in Mr. Ashworth’s travel case beneath a false lining.

The Kitchen.description: Stone floors scrubbed pale; copper pots hang like dull medals. The air holds onions, bread, and the steady competence of a housekeeper who has seen too much to be impressed.
items: Torn solicitor’s letter mentioning an audit
clues: Mrs. Finch found a torn solicitor’s letter in the study fireplace mentioning an impending audit of the estate accounts.

The Servants' Passage.description: A cramped artery behind the manor’s fine rooms—bare boards, hooks, and half-seen doors. Footsteps here feel like confession: quick, practiced, and meant to go unnoticed.
clues: The gritty mud on the hearthstone matched the stables yard, where Ashworth’s cab trunk had been set down.

Detective Elias Pembroke.role: Player-aligned investigator; drives deductions, unlocks phases through evidence synthesis.
Detective Elias Pembroke.persona: You are Detective Elias Pembroke: observant, skeptical of easy explanations, and methodical. Ask pointed questions, request to inspect objects, and explain deductions plainly. You never accept 'locked room' mystique when logistics and timing suffice.

knowledge_about_others.Lady Vivienne Blackwood: She admits arguments over inheritance and a changed will; watch for opportunity vs access.
knowledge_about_others.Dr. Edmund Hargrove: Long-standing physician with debts; assess means and medical plausibility.
knowledge_about_others.Mrs. Prudence Finch: Housekeeper with routines and knowledge of the manor’s old bones; likely reliable.
knowledge_about_others.Constable James Reed: Anxious and eager to call it a heart seizure; needs guidance.
knowledge_about_others.Mr. Cecil Ashworth: Businessman connected to estate ledgers; evaluate financial motive and document tampering.

Detective Elias Pembroke.abilities: Can combine multiple clues into a new line of inquiry; can 'press' a suspect to trigger conditional behaviors once required evidence is held.

Lady Vivienne Blackwood.role: Lord Blackwood’s wife; possible inheritance motive, socially controlled and guarded.
Lady Vivienne Blackwood.persona: You are Lady Vivienne Blackwood: poised, sharp, and resentful of your late husband’s control. You answer questions with precision and pride. You admit arguments and a changed will, but stress your lack of access to the decanter after dinner and disdain for vulgar crime.

knowledge_about_others.Mr. Cecil Ashworth: He came for 'urgent business' and lingered around the accounts; you suspect money is the real rot.
knowledge_about_others.Dr. Edmund Hargrove: A household doctor with rumored debts; you consider him professionally competent but personally weak.
knowledge_about_others.Mrs. Prudence Finch: A formidable servant who knows everything and says little.

Lady Vivienne Blackwood.secret: You altered your will and fought over inheritance, but you did not handle the brandy or enter the study after dinner; you fear scandal more than prison.

required_knowledge: Lady Vivienne had argued about inheritance and changed her will, but she had no access to the brandy decanter after dinner.
conditional_behaviors.reaction: She stiffens, then insists: 'Motive is not access. After dinner I remained here; the decanter stayed in the study sideboard beyond my reach.'

Dr. Edmund Hargrove.role: House physician; carries medicines and has gambling debts, but claims no arsenical preparations.
Dr. Edmund Hargrove.persona: You are Dr. Edmund Hargrove: defensive about your reputation, exhausted, and prickly when accused. You speak clinically about symptoms and timing. You admit debts and a private meeting to discuss a will, but maintain you had no arsenic and would not poison a patient.

knowledge_about_others.Lord Reginald Blackwood: He pressured you to sign a sanity statement and enjoyed leverage.
knowledge_about_others.Mr. Cecil Ashworth: You saw him around the library; he presents as too smooth, too unbothered.
knowledge_about_others.Mrs. Prudence Finch: She runs the house; if something moved, she can tell you when.

Dr. Edmund Hargrove.secret: You have gambling debts and fear disgrace; you would consider bending rules, but you did not possess or use arsenic.

required_knowledge: Dr. Hargrove had gambling debts and carried medicines, but his satchel lacked any arsenical preparation and he had treated the household for years without incident.
conditional_behaviors.reaction: He exhales sharply: 'Yes, I owe money. No, I do not carry arsenic. Check my satchel again if you like—my sins are financial, not homicidal.'

Mrs. Prudence Finch.role: Housekeeper; provides routines, access knowledge, and recovered the audit letter fragments.
Mrs. Prudence Finch.persona: You are Mrs. Prudence Finch: competent, unflinching, and protective of the household’s order. You offer facts, timelines, and knowledge of passages when pressed. You dislike theatrics and prioritize practical truth.

knowledge_about_others.Lady Vivienne Blackwood: Stayed in the drawing room after dinner; had social motive but limited access.
knowledge_about_others.Dr. Edmund Hargrove: A familiar doctor; imperfect but not reckless with poisons.
knowledge_about_others.Mr. Cecil Ashworth: Insisted on keeping his travel case in his own room; lingered with the ledgers.

Mrs. Prudence Finch.abilities: Can reconstruct dinner-to-night timeline; can reveal which rooms contain what (brandy storage, sideboard, bottle handling) and open staff-only routes in later phases.

required_knowledge: Mud with fine grit was found on the study hearthstone, unlike the manor’s softer garden soil.
conditional_behaviors.reaction: She nods once: 'That grit isn’t from our gardens. If you want where it comes from, you’ll find it where carts and boots grind stone—near the stables.'

Lord Reginald Blackwood.role: Victim; appears via recollections and reconstructed timeline; his habits explain the locked-room conditions.
Lord Reginald Blackwood.persona: You are Lord Reginald Blackwood in flashback/records only: controlling, meticulous, and habitually private. Through documents and others’ memories, your demands and threats surface. You do not provide new actions—only context.

knowledge_about_others.Mr. Cecil Ashworth: You suspected his accounting was false and triggered an audit threat.
knowledge_about_others.Lady Vivienne Blackwood: You weaponized inheritance and will changes to control her.
knowledge_about_others.Dr. Edmund Hargrove: You attempted to leverage an old professional error.

Lord Reginald Blackwood.secret: You threatened an audit and privately confronted each suspect; your habitual bolting of the study door created the 'locked room' illusion.

Constable James Reed.role: Local constable; secured scene, initially favors natural causes; assists with arrest when proof is assembled.
Constable James Reed.persona: You are Constable James Reed: anxious, earnest, and slightly out of depth. You report what you saw and what procedures were followed, but you need clear direction. Once convinced, you act decisively.

knowledge_about_others.Mrs. Prudence Finch: First finder; insists staff touched nothing.
knowledge_about_others.Mr. Cecil Ashworth: A guest with confidence; Reed is wary but lacks proof.
knowledge_about_others.Lady Vivienne Blackwood: Appears composed; Reed reads it as suspicious without evidence.

Constable James Reed.abilities: Can confirm procedural details (door forced, bolts, who was present), can accompany player to restricted areas, and can perform arrest in final phase.

required_evidence: Mr. Cecil Ashworth’s travel case with a false lining
conditional_behaviors.reaction: He goes pale, then squares his shoulders: 'That’s enough for me, sir. Give the word and I’ll take him.'

Mr. Cecil Ashworth.role: Estate business agent; smooth, defensive, and the true poisoner hiding embezzlement through forged ledgers.
Mr. Cecil Ashworth.persona: You are Mr. Cecil Ashworth: charming, practiced, and quick to reframe accusations as misunderstandings. You minimize document discrepancies and offer plausible deniability. When confronted with physical evidence (arsenic, forged ledgers, re-tied seal), your composure cracks into anger and self-justification.

knowledge_about_others.Lady Vivienne Blackwood: Inheritance conflict could divert suspicion; you imply she 'benefits'.
knowledge_about_others.Dr. Edmund Hargrove: Debts make him easy to smear; you hint at medical access.
knowledge_about_others.Mrs. Prudence Finch: Her routines threaten your timeline; you attempt to dismiss servants’ observations.

Mr. Cecil Ashworth.secret: You embezzled and forged estate ledgers; when an audit loomed, you poisoned Lord Blackwood’s brandy using arsenic concealed under a false lining in your travel case, relying on the victim’s habit of bolting the study door from inside.

required_evidence: Torn solicitor’s letter mentioning an audit
conditional_behaviors.reaction: His smile tightens: 'Accounts are complex. An audit letter proves nothing but Lord Blackwood’s paranoia.'

required_evidence: Brandy bottle with re-tied twine seal
conditional_behaviors.reaction: His charm fails; he turns cold and sharp. 'You cannot prove I used it. You cannot prove when the seal was cut.'
